concepts.hook: Ithúna, a girl drowned off the Skarel rocks, was sent aloft on a kite her mother flew until the string parted, so the kite now hangs in the Unflown where her mother still looks for it.
Varo sailed past the last water anyone had charted and never came back, and his boat-lantern still burns in the south, so sailors claim to see it when they are lost.

concepts.gloss: The Net That Came Up Light
concepts.hook: Mesket tried to copy Kael and cast for fallen stars, hauled up a net holding one lantern and no stone, and the lantern and the net were left in the Unflown as a warning.
After Aun cut the string he dropped the sheath of his knife, and the loop of stars that marks it lies in the Unflown where the knife's spark was struck.
Sil, the Drowned Lantern, walks the Unflown each season carrying a single lamp, and the one star that shifts its place each year is her light searching for Aun.
When Orrun shifted under the islands he sank one arch of his ribs into the south, and the bones show as a row of pale stars that the Gulls say are still settling.
Hesk, who counts every string, once let a loose thread fall from the Reel and never counted it, so it hangs in the Unflown as the one thing she has not kept track of.
Tavo laughed so hard at a sailor's joke that a gust took the sailor's cap out over the sea, and the red cap now rolls around the southern sky while Tavo claims it was never his.
Ennu began a gull from cloth and bone for a grieving widow, stopped when the widow died, and left the bird with one wing unstitched, which the stars still show as a gap.
Óllun sailed south to find the end of the wind, reached the Unflown, and turned his boat around, so the lantern on his mast now points toward home while his stars face the wrong way.
Skelra, a rower who was too proud to lift her oar out of a storm, lost it when it split, and its two halves drift in the Unflown as a pair of stars that never meet.
Hasla, an old knot-wife of the first village, tied a bowline no tide could loosen, and the Unflown shows its loops as a cluster of stars that have never slipped.
Ammel lowered a weighted line into the southern dark to measure how far the sky went down, and the line has been falling ever since, so the stars along it grow fainter toward the bottom.
Two Gulls were sent south with a message for the drowned, argued about the words on the way, and fell silent in the Unflown still holding the message between them.
A child's whistle made from a seabird's wing-bone was blown from a cliff in a gale and lost to the south, and in the Unflown its faint star is said to sound only when the wind is wrong.
Every year Mitha climbs the rock above the harbour to light a lamp for a son who went south in a boat, and his star in the Unflown flickers on the same night each year, as if answering.

concepts.gloss: The Net With Nothing In It
concepts.hook: Kael casts his net into the south sky each night and draws it back empty, and the net's open mesh is the constellation, a lace of stars with no fallen light caught inside.

concepts.gloss: The Ship in Its Own Wake
concepts.hook: A voyager's boat sailed so far south that it came around the pole and met its own wake, so the pair of stars that mark the boat and its trail are always chasing each other.
Ostrel, a fisherman known for his lies, told the tale of a catch so often that the fish grew too big for the harbour and was thrown into the Unflown, where its bones are still too large for the sky.
Ennu built a kite once that stayed up with no string at all, and the constellation shows the kite alone in the dark, which the Kite-Wright sometimes says was a mistake of the wind.
In one night Tavo wrecked eleven voyagers' sailboats off the southern reef, and their sails, tattered and pale, still hang in the Unflown in a loose row like washing that no one came back for.
Aun kept a small fire alight on his boat after he cut the string, and it is the only spark from his knife that never went out, now glowing in the south as a lamp no one sits beside.
Kenna's goat walked off the cliff path chasing a gull, fell all the way down to the sea, and was flung into the Unflown, where its horned outline is the only star-shape that still looks surprised.
A lost man asked the Gulls the way home and was told three different roads, so the stars that mark each road sit at angles to one another, and every sailor who looks at them takes a different path.
Mesket held a rope across an ice-crack to pull a man out, her hands froze to it, and the rope burned out through her fingers, leaving a short thread of stars that ends in an open hand.

concepts.gloss: The Mourning Kite of Two Sisters
concepts.hook: Two sisters flew a mourning kite south for their father, one tying the tail and the other holding the string, and the kite now hangs in the Unflown with its two tails trailing toward the islands.

concepts.gloss: The Cut End of the String
concepts.hook: The piece of string Aun held when he cut the sky free is still knotted to nothing, and its short loose end is the faint line of stars that every drowned sailor is told to follow.

A helmsman who drowned with his crew was never named by the islanders, because the Ilvari believe a name said aloud calls a boat back, so his star is the one dark-edged lamp in the Unflown with no name attached.

When Orrun turned in his sleep the harbour village of Hessa slid off his back into the south, and its houses, drawn in lamplight, still show as a small crooked cluster that people call the town of lost doors.
